disclaimer: Reminder reference only — NOT legal authority. Season dates, zones, limits, and quotas are set annually and can change; bobcat/fisher/otter seasons may close early when quotas are reached. Always verify current regulations with the Wisconsin DNR before hunting or trapping.

license_summary.general: A Wisconsin trapping license (trapping authorization) is required to trap. Bobcat requires a bobcat permit + pelt tag from the annual drawing (application deadline Aug. 1). Fisher and river otter require a current valid harvest authorization from the department (NR 10.145). Harvest registration via GameReg; CITES certification applies to bobcat and otter pelts.

species.notes: Bobcat hunting/trapping only by permit drawing (application deadline Aug. 1). Permit is valid only in the area and time period specified. Pelt tag must be sealed immediately mouth-to-eye when the animal is killed. Harvest must be registered via GameReg by 5 p.m. the day after recovery; pelt presented to a DNR warden within 7 days after the month of harvest for certification and CITES tag. North/South zone boundary is approximately State Highway 64.
permit_requirements: Current and valid bobcat permit and pelt tag from the annual drawing required; one bobcat per permit (2025 regs structure; 2026 permit structure confirmed by DNR dates page).
Immediately validate and attach/seal the pelt tag through the mouth-to-eye openings.
Register the harvest via GameReg by 5 p.m. the day after recovery.

Present the skinned pelt to a DNR warden or authorized staff within 7 days after the month of harvest for certification (CITES tag). No raw bobcat pelt may be possessed longer than 7 days after the month of harvest without certification; no transfer/sale of a raw pelt without the certification seal.

species.notes: As of 2020 there is no longer a drawing for otters — otters are a bag limit/quota species. A current and valid otter harvest authorization is required (NR 10.145). River otters are a CITES Appendix II species. A statewide harvest quota applies and the season may close early — check the DNR hotline (855-299-9653) before trapping.
permit_requirements: Current and valid otter harvest authorization required.
Season limit: one otter per harvest authorization; authorizations are valid statewide (2025 regs structure).
Register the harvest via GameReg by 5 p.m. the day following recovery. A CITES tag is mailed to the trapper; it must be immediately affixed to the head portion of the pelt upon receipt.
No raw otter pelt may be possessed after the 7th day of the month following season closure without a certification seal; no transfer/sale of a raw pelt without the seal (NR 10.087).
